extracted.intended_audience: faculty, researchers, and grant writers preparing NSF proposals (and reviewers assessing them)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance describing the National Science Foundation's two merit review criteria (Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts), related considerations (integration of research and education, diversity), and expectations for proposers and reviewers when preparing and evaluating NSF proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the intellectual merit of the proposed activity?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations (suggestions; not all will apply): How important is the proposed activity to advancing knowledge and understanding within its own field or across different fields? How well qualified is the proposer (individual or team) to conduct the project? (If appropriate, the reviewer will comment on the quality of prior work.) To what extent does the proposed activity suggest and explore creative and original concepts? How well conceived and organized is the proposed activity? Is there sufficient access to resources?

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the broader impacts of the proposed activity?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations (suggestions; not all will apply): How well does the activity advance discovery and understanding while promoting teaching, training, and learning? How well does the proposed activity broaden the participation of underrepresented groups (e.g., gender, ethnicity, disability, geographic, etc.)? To what extent will it enhance the infrastructure for research and education, such as facilities, instrumentation, networks, and partnerships? Will the results be disseminated broadly to enhance scientific and technological understanding? What may be the benefits of the proposed activity to society?

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of Research and Education
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration of research and education is a principal NSF strategy to foster its goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions provide opportunities for individuals to assume concurrent responsibilities as researchers, educators, and students; engage in joint efforts that infuse education with the excitement of discovery; and enrich research through the diversity of learning perspectives. Reviewers and proposers should consider how the project integrates research and education activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrating Diversity into Programs, Projects, and Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadening opportunities and enabling participation of all citizens (women and men, underrepresented minorities, persons with disabilities, geographic diversity, etc.) is essential and central to NSF-supported programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should address how they broaden participation and inclusivity. Reviewers should evaluate contributions to diversity as part of broader impacts where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program- or Solicitation-Specific Additional Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF may employ additional criteria as required to highlight the specific objectives of certain programs and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some solicitations (e.g., large facility projects) include special review criteria in the program solicitation. Proposers must consult the relevant solicitation; reviewers should apply additional criteria only when specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Considerations and Reviewer Scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The listed considerations are suggestions and not all will apply to every proposal; reviewers will only be asked to address considerations relevant to the proposal and for which they are qualified to make judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers must address both merit review criteria in their submission, but reviewers should limit their comments to applicable considerations and their areas of expertise. This affects what aspects get evaluated and how feedback should be framed.
